lens: Dasatinib's 50% efficacy rate in DLBCL cell lines masks a binary response pattern that likely reflects uncharacterized molecular subtypes, while its senolytic properties (hinted in aging studies) propose a dual role in hematologic malignancies and age-related pathways, but the evidence is too fragmented for a cohesive thesis.
known_to_ignore: Dasatinib shows efficacy in 50% of DLBCL cell lines
tensions: The 50% efficacy in DLBCL cells contrasts with near-universal resistance in solid tumors, yet no resistance mechanisms are identified in the available data
gaps: DLBCL cell line subtypes (e.g., ABC vs. GCB) not stratified for dasatinib response
Lack of in vivo or clinical data on dasatinib for DLBCL
No integration of dasatinib's senolytic effects with lymphoma biology
reviewer_objections: Only a single cell-line study is cited, insufficient for generalizability
No mechanistic or clinical evidence to support a translational narrative
next_extractions: Dasatinib sensitivity in specific DLBCL subtypes (e.g., MCD or EZB genetic subtypes)
Senolytic impacts of dasatinib on p53/miR34a in lymphoma models
Combination regimens with quercetin for DLBCL, leveraging aging pathway data
